reasoning: The deepseek model successfully audited all 6 files and found them to be standard, benign AUR packaging. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' verdict was due to API errors (HTTP 400) on 2 files, not security findings. All reviewed files show normal AUR patterns: PKGBUILD fetches from official Google domains with checksums, .install script only prints messages, wrapper script reads user config, and other files are metadata/config. No malicious injection detected.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from infrastructure failures, not security analysis. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing eula_text.html and google-chrome-beta.install, forcing an 'inconclusive' verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. The openrouter report (advisory: true) also had a parsing error on .SRCINFO but doesn't count as a vote.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit eula_text.html and google-chrome-beta.install due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
openrouter model failed to parse decision for .SRCINFO
learnings: API errors (HTTP 400, timeouts) should trigger automatic retry or fallback to another model rather than marking files as 'inconclusive'
When one model completes a full audit successfully and another's 'inconclusive' is due to tool errors (not security findings), the successful audit should take precedence in the final verdict
Implement stricter output format validation and parsing for LLM responses to avoid 'could not parse a decision' errors
Consider implementing a consensus mechanism where tool failures don't block a verdict if other models have successfully audited the same files
